01.event: a bill of divorce signed by Anan bar Hiyya of Neharde'a is found in Sura; the Sages search from Sura to Neharde'a and find only Anan bar Hiyya of Hagra
01.turn: witnesses testify that Anan bar Hiyya of Hagra was with them in Neharde'a on the day it was written
01.outcome: none narrated; Abaye and Rava argue whether to be concerned
01.summary: A bill of divorce turns up in Sura naming Anan bar Hiyya of Neharde'a. The Sages search the region and find only one man of that name, but witnesses say he was in Neharde'a that day. Abaye and Rava then debate whether the document may still be his.
01.missing: what was done with the bill; any resolution
01.reason: There are real events (the find, the search, the testimony) but nothing changes; the passage ends in a legal debate, so it is part of a story rather than a full one.

02.event: he claimed his money belonged to a gentile to avoid paying
02.turn: the Sages acted improperly with him in return
02.outcome: he was forced to sell his land to pay
02.summary: Rav Hama explains the incident behind Rava's ruling: a debtor hid his money by attributing it to a gentile, so the Sages forced him to sell his land.
02.missing: the incident is only summarized inside a dialogue about attribution; no detail
02.reason: An incident with an act and a response is recalled, but only sketched within a dialogue about a ruling's attribution; alluded rather than narrated.

03.missing: the story itself is in the preceding context; this is commentary on it
03.reason: Rabbi Abba's addition that Nehunya's son died of thirst is the Gemara's comment on the story, supported by verse exegesis, not a story of its own.

04.missing: any narrated detail of the incident
04.reason: A baraita mentions that an uncircumcised priest once sprinkled and the Sages validated it: one bare event plus a ruling, which is not a story.

05.event: funerals had become so costly that relatives abandoned their dead and fled
05.turn: Rabban Gamliel had himself buried in plain linen
05.outcome: all the people followed his example; today even cheap cloth is used
05.summary: Burial costs grew so ruinous that families abandoned their dead. Rabban Gamliel ordered that he be buried in simple linen, and the whole people followed him, changing the custom.
05.reason: A situation, a sage's deliberate act, and a resulting change in what everyone did: several actions with causality and change.

06.actor: a man taken captive with his mother
06.event: he and his mother were captured by gentiles; he remarks incidentally that he never left her
06.outcome: Rabbi permits the mother to marry a priest on the basis of his remark
06.summary: A man, chatting without intent to testify, says he and his mother were held captive and he never let her out of his mind. The case came before Rabbi, who married her into the priesthood on his word.
06.reason: The captivity is told only in the man's remark and the rest is a ruling; but the ruling is an act that changes her status (marriage into the priesthood), which keeps it borderline rather than not.

07.turn: delayed selling it until the Festival
07.summary: Rav Kahana, holding beer belonging to an orphan, waited until the Festival to sell it, explaining that it would fetch cash then.
07.reason: A report of what a sage did, cited as practice with his reasoning; nothing follows, so it is a bare report.

08.actor: residents of a crooked alley in Sura
08.event: they placed a rolled-up mat at the bend as a side post
08.summary: Residents of a bent alley in Sura used a rolled mat as a side post, and Rav Hisda said it was valid under neither Rav nor Shmuel.
08.reason: One act followed by a ruling and its legal reasoning; nothing else changes.

09.actor: Rav Pappa and Yehuda bar Mareimar
09.event: Rav Pappa goes to write his son's bride's ketuba; Yehuda bar Mareimar comes out to greet him
09.turn: at the door Yehuda takes his leave; Rav Pappa invites him in
09.summary: Rav Pappa arranged his son's marriage into Abba of Sura's family and went to write the ketuba. Yehuda bar Mareimar came out to honor him but turned away at the door, and Rav Pappa urged him to come in.
09.missing: his reluctance explained and the resolution, in the following segment
09.reason: Several narrated actions by named sages with an emerging tension; the passage is the opening of a story that continues past it.

10.event: they send the question to Rav with the names of Shmuel and Karna reversed
10.turn: Rav swears that she needs both a get and refusal
10.outcome: Rav defends the view he thinks is not Shmuel's
10.summary: Instead of asking Mar Ukva, the Sages sent the question to Rav, swapping who said what. Rav swore by God that she needs both, and that Shmuel's line should never say otherwise.
10.missing: the payoff (that Rav endorsed Shmuel's view) is implied, not narrated
10.reason: Mainly speech and a sent question, with a ruse and a pointed oath giving some conflict; speech-dominated, so borderline.

11.event: he stipulates that a get takes effect if he does not return within thirty days
11.turn: he arrives at the last moment but the ferry keeps him on the far bank; he shouts that he has come
11.outcome: Shmuel rules it does not count as a return; the divorce takes effect
11.summary: A man made his divorce conditional on not returning within thirty days. On the last day he reached the river but could not cross, and shouted to the people on the other side that he had come. Shmuel ruled that this was not a return.
11.reason: Something happens to someone (stranded by the ferry), he responds, and a ruling resolves it with real consequence: the incident-plus-ruling shape R-C0 accepts.

12.reason: A harmonization of two statements by dating them before and after Rav came to Babylonia; no event is narrated.

13.event: his brother's widow lives in Bei Hoza'a; he asks Rabbi Hanina whether to go down and marry her
13.summary: A man asked Rabbi Hanina whether he could go to Babylonia for levirate marriage. Rabbi Hanina answered that his brother had left, married a 'Samaritan' and died, so why follow him?
13.missing: whether the man went or stayed
13.reason: A setting plus a question and an answer; the sharp reply is ordinary rabbinic speech and nothing further happens.

14.actor: a millstone owner and his renter
14.event: a man rents a millstone in exchange for grinding services
14.turn: the owner grows rich, buys his own millstone and donkey, and demands money instead
14.outcome: the renter refuses, offering only grinding (resolution follows in the discussion)
14.summary: A man rented out his millstone in return for grinding. He later got rich, bought another millstone and a donkey, and demanded cash rent; the renter insisted he had only agreed to grind.
14.missing: the ruling, which follows in the context
14.reason: Several actions (renting, becoming rich, buying) cause a change and a dispute between the parties: an incident, not a hypothetical, of R-C0's cow shape.

15.event: a man leaves his property to Toviya and dies
15.turn: a Toviya comes to claim it
15.outcome: Rabbi Yohanan rules that Toviya has come and takes it
15.summary: A man on his deathbed left his estate to Toviya and died. Toviya appeared, and Rabbi Yohanan ruled the property his without worrying about another Toviya.
15.reason: A few real events (the bequest, the death, the claimant's arrival) but they mainly set up a ruling; between borderline and not, borderline.

16.actor: Mar Zutra and a rebellious wife
16.event: a woman refused her husband out of disgust
16.turn: Mar Zutra compelled her to stay
16.outcome: Rabbi Hanina of Sura was born of the couple
16.summary: A wife rebelled, saying her husband disgusted her, and Mar Zutra forced her to stay. From that couple came Rabbi Hanina of Sura, though the Gemara attributes that to heavenly help.
16.missing: detail; the incident is only mentioned as a precedent
16.reason: Events and a change (a child) are mentioned, but the incident is only alluded to as a precedent and immediately discounted by the Gemara.

17.event: serves drinks at his son Abba Mar's wedding
17.turn: Rav Yitzhak son of Rav Yehuda does not stand for him
17.summary: At his son's wedding Rav Pappa poured a cup for Rav Yitzhak son of Rav Yehuda, who did not rise before him, and Rav Pappa took offense.
17.reason: Real actions and an emotional reaction (which counts as an event), but minimal development, cited only as an anecdote to raise a difficulty.

18.missing: any event beyond reporting a ruling, praise and rebuke
18.reason: Ravnai reports Shmuel's ruling, Ameimar praises it and Rav Ashi rebukes him: standard rabbinic dialogue, which Jeff ruled not a story on this very passage.

19.event: his relatives must pay for their father's widow's daily treatment
19.turn: he advises them to fix a lump sum with the doctor, so the cost comes out of her ketuba
19.outcome: he later regrets it: 'we made ourselves like legal advisors'
19.summary: Rabbi Yohanan's relatives faced their stepmother's daily medical bills. He told them to agree a fixed fee with the doctor so it would come from her ketuba, and later regretted acting as their legal advisor.
19.reason: A case brought to a rabbi with advice, but followed by a change in him (regret); more than a ruling, though it is mainly speech, so borderline.

20.event: the sons of Yudan the maidservant are freed
20.turn: Rav Aha permits them to marry each other's wives; Rava challenges him
20.outcome: Rav Aha retorts that he permits what Rav Sheshet forbade
20.summary: When the freed sons of Yudan asked, Rav Aha bar Ya'akov permitted them to marry each other's ex-wives. Rava objected that Rav Sheshet forbade it; Rav Aha replied that he disagreed.
20.missing: any narrated outcome beyond the ruling
20.reason: One event (the manumission), a ruling, and ordinary scholarly back-and-forth; nothing further changes.
